key_insight: Neural approximation power alone cannot ensure PINN convergence: discrete residuals must control continuous error within stable admissible trial classes.
engineering_relevance: For linear elliptic Dirichlet PDEs, the framework guides collocation-point requirements and scale-dependent, physics-balanced boundary weighting.
method: Extend kernel collocation theory using elliptic regularity, discrete stability, and consistency.
Identify admissible neural subclasses whose continuous residuals are controlled by discrete loss.
Construct admissible tanh-MLP comparison networks to establish constrained convergence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence results, including conditional unconstrained convergence under joint network and sampling refinement, but no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Unconstrained PINN convergence remains conditional; expressive networks alone do not guarantee the required stability and consistency.
paper_title: Stable admissible neural classes and convergent physics-informed neural networks
